text: A girl on a scooter travels at a constant velocity of 2.0 m s–1. Calculate the final velocity of the scooter if she accelerates at 0.5 m s–2 for 6 s. Show working. (3 marks)
html: A girl on a scooter travels at a constant velocity of 2.0 m s–1. Calculate the final velocity of the scooter if she accelerates at 0.5 m s–2 for 6 s. Show working. (3 marks)
answerHtml:
Worked solution

Given u = 2.0 m/s, a = 0.5 m/s² and t = 6 s. [1] v = u + at = 2.0 + 0.5(6). [1] v = 5.0 m/s in the original direction. [1]

Worked solution

Convert v = 60/3.6 = 16.6667 m/s. [1] Eₖ = ½mv² = 0.5 × 1100 × 16.6667². [1] Eₖ = 152,778 J ≈ 1.53 × 10⁵ J. [1]

text: The type of wings a fly has can be represented by NN, Nn, or nn. N is the allele for normal wings and n is the allele for dumpy wings. (a) Why do we use capital letters for some alleles and lower case for others? (1 mark) (b) Why are there two letters for each genotype? (1mark)
html:
The type of wings a fly has can be represented by NN, Nn, or nn. N is the allele for normal wings and n is the allele for dumpy wings.

(a) Why do we use capital letters for some alleles and lower case for others?

(1 mark)

(b) Why are there two letters for each genotype?

(1mark)
answerHtml:
Worked solution

(a) Capital N represents the dominant allele and lower-case n the recessive allele; Nn shows normal wings in this model. [1]

(b) A diploid fly has two alleles at the locus, one inherited from each parent. [1]

text: Errors during DNA replication can cause mutations, and different germline cell lineages undergo different numbers of divisions. (a) Which cell division produces sperm and eggs? [1] (b) Describe three differences between mitosis and meiosis. [3] (c) Define mutation. [1] (d) Explain how increased heritable mutation could increase the variation available for evolutionary change. [2]
html: Errors during DNA replication can cause mutations, and different germline cell lineages undergo different numbers of divisions. (a) Which cell division produces sperm and eggs? [1] (b) Describe three differences between mitosis and meiosis. [3] (c) Define mutation. [1] (d) Explain how increased heritable mutation could increase the variation available for evolutionary change. [2]
answerHtml:
Worked solution

(a) Meiosis. [1]

(b) Mitosis has one nuclear division, meiosis two; mitosis usually gives two genetically similar diploid cells, meiosis four varied haploid products; homologous pairing/crossing over occur in meiosis but not normal mitosis. [3, one per paired difference]

(c) A mutation is a change in genetic material, such as the DNA sequence. [1]

(d) More heritable mutations can supply more new alleles and variation. [1] Selection can change variant frequencies over generations if reproductive success differs. [1] Mutation does not guarantee faster adaptation: many changes are neutral or harmful.

text: In 2005 a space telescope detected a star that exploded 13 billion years ago. The light from the star shows the biggest red-shift ever measured. 1. What is red-shift? (1 mark) 2. What does the measurement of its red-shift tell scientists about this star? (1 mark) (c) Red-shift provides evidence for the ‘big bang’ theory. Describe the ‘big bang’ theory. (2 marks)
html:
In 2005 a space telescope detected a star that exploded 13 billion years ago. The light from the star shows the biggest red-shift ever measured. 1. What is red-shift? (1 mark) 2. What does the measurement of its red-shift tell scientists about this star? (1 mark)

(c) Red-shift provides evidence for the ‘big bang’ theory.

Describe the ‘big bang’ theory. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Worked solution

(a) Redshift is a shift of spectral features to longer wavelengths than their laboratory values. [1]

(b) A very large cosmological redshift indicates light emitted in a much earlier, less-expanded universe, supporting great distance and substantial cosmic expansion along its path. [1]

(c) The Big Bang model describes expansion from a hot, dense early state. [1] Expansion cooled the universe, allowing atoms and later stars and galaxies to form. [1] It is not an ordinary explosion into pre-existing empty space.
